applies_why: This judge text does the thing the rule governs by assigning UNDERDETERMINED to D4 vs C2 based on the two father-references in Luke 2:48-49.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand." I weighed reading 1: Luke 2:48-49 has two father-references and is open/underdetermined; reading 2: both senses stand and the verse is not open.
why: Under K-S2, because the verse carries both senses, both stand and it is not open, so the judge's UNDERDETERMINED label breaches the rule.
